Option D is single-Region. Option E is not feasible across Regions due to latency.

stem: A DevOps engineer needs to implement end-to-end request tracing for an application that uses API Gateway, Lambda, SQS, and another Lambda function for async processing. Standard X-Ray tracing loses the trace context when crossing the SQS queue boundary. How should tracing be maintained?

options.text: Enable X-Ray active tracing on all Lambda functions and API Gateway. When sending messages to SQS, include the X-Ray trace header (AWSTraceHeader) as an SQS message system attribute. The downstream Lambda function extracts the trace header from the SQS message and uses it to continue the trace. This creates a connected trace across the asynchronous boundary.
Use separate traces for the synchronous and asynchronous parts.
Replace SQS with a synchronous Lambda invocation.
Use CloudWatch Logs correlation IDs instead of X-Ray.

explanation: SQS supports the AWSTraceHeader message system attribute which carries X-Ray trace context across the queue boundary. The downstream Lambda function automatically picks up this trace context, creating a connected trace from API Gateway through SQS to the processing Lambda. This maintains end-to-end visibility. Option B breaks the trace context. Option C changes the architecture. Option D provides correlation but not visual trace maps.

stem: A company needs to implement a war room communication protocol for major incidents. When a P1 incident is declared, the system should automatically create a dedicated communication channel, page the incident commander, start recording a timeline, and begin collecting relevant metrics snapshots. Which AWS service orchestrates this?

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Incident Manager with response plans. Configure the response plan to: engage the on-call incident commander via PagerDuty or SNS, create an AWS Chatbot Slack channel for the incident, start a timeline that automatically records actions, and execute an SSM Automation runbook that captures CloudWatch metric snapshots for the affected services.
Use a shared email thread for incident communication.
Create a manual checklist for incident managers to follow.
Use CloudWatch dashboards as the primary incident management tool.

explanation: Incident Manager provides structured incident management with automated response plans. Engagements page the right people. Chatbot integration creates dedicated communication channels. Timelines track all actions automatically. SSM Automation captures diagnostic data. This provides a comprehensive, automated P1 incident response process. Option B lacks structure. Option C is manual. Option D is monitoring only.

stem: A DevOps engineer needs to implement a solution that monitors and alerts on changes to critical IAM resources (root user activity, IAM policy changes, new IAM users, role assumption from unusual IPs). Which monitoring approach provides the MOST comprehensive IAM security monitoring?

options.text: Configure CloudTrail to log all IAM management events. Create EventBridge rules that match specific IAM API calls: CreateUser, AttachUserPolicy, CreateAccessKey, ConsoleLogin for root user, and AssumeRole. Each rule triggers Lambda functions or SNS notifications for alerting. Use GuardDuty to detect unusual IAM activity patterns including credential compromise and unauthorized access.
Review CloudTrail logs weekly for IAM changes.
Use IAM Access Analyzer only for external access detection.
Monitor IAM credential reports monthly.

explanation: EventBridge rules on specific CloudTrail IAM events provide real-time alerting for critical IAM changes. GuardDuty adds ML-based anomaly detection for credential compromise and unusual access patterns. Together they provide comprehensive, real-time IAM security monitoring. Option B is too infrequent. Option C only detects external sharing. Option D is monthly and limited to credential status.

stem: A DevOps team wants to implement a GitOps approach for managing their AWS infrastructure. All infrastructure changes must be tracked in Git, reviewed via pull requests, and applied automatically when merged. Manual AWS console changes should be detected and alerted. Which architecture implements this?

options.text: Store all CloudFormation/CDK templates in a Git repository. Use CodePipeline triggered by repository merges to apply infrastructure changes. Require pull request approvals with CodeBuild running cfn-lint and cfn-guard for validation. Use AWS Config with custom rules or CloudFormation drift detection to identify manual changes. Alert on drift via EventBridge and SNS. Optionally auto-remediate drift by re-running the pipeline.
Use the AWS console for all infrastructure changes and commit screenshots to Git.
Allow both Git-based and console changes without tracking.
Use Terraform Cloud exclusively without AWS-native tools.

explanation: This implements full GitOps: Git as the source of truth, PR reviews for governance, automated deployment via CodePipeline, policy validation with cfn-lint/cfn-guard, and drift detection to catch manual changes. Auto-remediation ensures infrastructure always matches Git. Option B does not implement GitOps. Option C lacks governance. Option D excludes AWS-native tools.
